input.question: How did the American Southern accent develop?
input.ground_truth: It's more the other way around, and relates to the question "When did American English break from British English?". At first American and British English were the same, but then British English developed into what it is today. American English has not changed as much, and is actually closer to British English of 200 years ago. American Southern has been even slower to change (because of the relative isolation of the speakers), and is even closer to British English of that time!

Question: How did the American Southern accent develop?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine a long, long time ago, people from England moved to a place called America. They lived in different parts of the new land. Some people moved to the south, where it was hot and there were lots of farms.

Because these people didn’t see or talk to people from other places very often, they started to talk a little bit differently. They made up their own way of saying words. This special way of talking is called an “accent.” 

Over many, many years, the people in the south kept talking this way, and it became the Southern accent! Just like how you sound a little different from your friends who live far away.
